title: Book One · Chapter 42: One Step Missing
story:
Mrs Lan agrees to try the boys' street map on Tuesday. She is going to the thread shop anyway. Mum will walk beside her. Mrs Lan will try to follow the map first. Then she can ask Mum for help.

Ronan carries a pencil to mark mistakes. Leo wants to carry the map. Mrs Lan needs to follow the map. So she carries it herself. Leo takes a spare pencil instead.

She holds it far from her glasses.

“That's a very round bird,” she says.

“Painted,” Leo explains.

“I hoped so.”

They go along River Street. Mrs Lan finds the bun shop. She finds Mr Qiu's stall. She finds the oil shop on the page. Beside it is a line. It looks like the lane. She turns there.

Ronan opens his mouth. He wants to correct her. Mum touches his shoulder lightly. He waits.

Mrs Lan stops at a closed wooden door.

“The map says through here.”

“No,” Leo says. “That's the wall.”

“Then why does it have the same line as the lane?”

The boys look. The wall and lane are both thin pencil lines. Their road line ends at the paper edge. There was no room for more road.

Ronan wants to explain their drawing. He looks from the map to the door. He looks at the line on the page. It points straight toward this door. It is exactly beside the mark for the oil shop. The page does not show the small gap between them.

“We need a wider lane,” he says.

“On the paper,” Mrs Lan says. “Please don't start moving my street.”

They laugh and go back to the right opening. Mrs Lan finds the thread shop after one more question. She points to the little step mark. “This helps,” she says. “It has the word STEP beside it now.”

Mum buys her chosen grey thread. The shopkeeper asks about the map. Leo shows it to her. His hands stay on the paper. He does not touch the clean cloth on the counter.

“My side door is not on your map,” she says.

“Does anyone use it?” Ronan asks.

“I do. Every morning.”

She points to the narrow passage behind the shop. Several families use it to reach their homes. It is not a road for everyone. The boys can mark that entrance. They must also write PRIVATE beside it. Other people must ask first. Then the shopkeeper can open the way for them.

They add a little short bar across that line. At home, Mum helps them explain their marks. Each mark gets a word beside it. One means road. Others mean door, private way, and step.

Leo draws a lock beside the private way. “That looks like a small bucket,” Ronan says. They keep the written words as well.

Mrs Lan tests the new version with her finger after dinner. This time, she doesn't enter the wall. “Which end has number six?” she asks.

Ronan leaves another question mark. They still need to check that place. But he wants to finish one part today.

Dad looks over Ronan's shoulder. “You have many doors,” he says. “Someone lives behind each of those doors.”

“People can move,” Ronan says.

“Signs can change, too. Check the sign and ask the person.”

The boys date the map. It is not a real city map, and they don't put it up for strangers to follow. Mrs Lan found the shop. She found a wrong turn on the map, too. Ronan writes both results on the back. Tomorrow they can read both.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：map＝地图；private＝私人的；entrance＝入口；step＝台阶。

理解问题：

1. Mrs Lan 按图走路时遇到了什么缺口？
2. 孩子们怎样改进街图，而不是责怪看图的人？
